text: Clipping workflow: paste a podcast or stream link, download at 1080p, cut the strongest 20 to 45 second moments, add captions, export 9:16 clips and write a review file before anything is posted.
Clip scoring ranks each moment by hook strength in the first three seconds, speaker energy, a clear payoff, and caption readability. Clips scoring under 60 are dropped and logged.
Lead finder: describe your ideal buyer, the swarm scans public directories, scores each lead by fit, writes a one line reason and queues a draft email. A human approves every send.
Property scout compares listing price with nearby sold prices, flags undervalued properties, and lists investors who bought similar homes in the area for a buy and flip.

Service arbitrage: find a service local businesses pay for, deliver it with automation at lower cost, and keep the margin. The workflow handles intake, delivery, invoice reminders and review requests.
Startup scout watches launch boards and funding news, matches new companies to your investment thesis, and builds a weekly list of founders worth a call.
Retention lab runs A/B tests on hooks, titles and thumbnails. It compares your average view duration with a competitor video on the same topic and keeps the version that holds viewers longer.
Translation engine localizes a pitch or video script into many languages, keeps product names untouched, and schedules each version for the right time zone.
Approvals: anything that posts, sends or spends money waits in a queue. Approve or deny with one tap. Nothing leaves the machine without a human yes.
MARVIN guide gives one next action at a time, speaks it out loud, and explains why it matters. Finish it, earn experience points, and the next action appears.

RPG layer turns tasks into monsters inside dungeons. Attack a task by finishing it. The last task in a dungeon is the boss, a critical strike unlocks a new workflow. PVE only, no player versus player.
Workflow ROI scores money earned against money spent, how repeatable the workflow is from one to ten, and hours of work. Losing workflows are killed, thin ones held, strong ones scaled.
Circuit breaker retries a stalled task three times, then reroutes to a fallback such as saving to an outbox and retrying through a second n8n node, so the run keeps going unattended.
Monthly vote: subscribers vote on the next hustle to add to the subscription at no extra cost. The winner ships with its course and its n8n workflows.
